guide_line: Count valence electrons and assign formal charge.
steps: Add the valence electrons of each atom. A group number is a good start: C 4, N 5, O 6, F 7, H 1.
Add one electron for each negative charge. Subtract one for each positive charge.
The less electronegative atom (never H) is the center. Connect the atoms, then fill octets.
Formal charge = valence electrons − lone-pair electrons − number of bonds.
Type the electron count, or the formal charge, as a number.

worked_example.q: How many valence electrons does CO2 have?

similar_problem.q: How many valence electrons does H2O have?

problems.q: How many valence electrons are in CO2?
problems.why: O=C=O. Each oxygen keeps two lone pairs.
hints: Add group numbers, then add electrons for a negative charge.

hints: Add group numbers, then add electrons for a negative charge.

problems.q: How many valence electrons are in NO3-?

problems.q: How many valence electrons are in CH2O?

problems.why: Add the 2− charge. Sulfur is the center with four S-O bonds in the octet form.
hints: Add group numbers, then add electrons for a negative charge.

hints: Add group numbers, then add electrons for a negative charge.

problems.q: How many valence electrons are in PCl5?

hints: Add group numbers, then add electrons for a negative charge.

problems.q: How many valence electrons are in CN-?

problems.q: Formal charge on O with 1 bond and 3 lone pairs?
problems.why: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons. Lone-pair electrons = 6. Bonds = 1. 6 − 6 − 1 = −1.
hints: Count lone-pair electrons, not the number of pairs.
